newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bonds seen quiet, rangebound to Monday.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bonds seen quiet, rangebound to Monday.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds which passed a rangebound day on Thursday, are expected to remain in the same pattern until Monday's OLO auction, traders said.
"There are no figures on Friday to influence the market," one trader said. "It will stay this way until the auction."
Traders reported steady business on the grey market in the new March 2007 linear bond that will be one of two lines on sale at Monday's monthly auction.
"It is well bid and expensive and will get more expensive," one trader said. He added that the spread over Bunds might widen slightly before Monday, but not by much.
Traders said the bond market had proved remarkably resilient to the twin shocks of higher-than-expected German M3 data and strong U.S. housing starts, dipping slightly both times but then recovering.
"There are simply no sellers. Everyone is buying at the moment," one trader said.
"I get the feeling that a number of portfolios out there are underweight. But once they are complete and the buying evaporates this market will collapse," another trader said.
The benchmark 2006 OLO was yielding an unchanged 6.38 percent and the spread over Bunds narrowed one tick to 21 bp.
The front month bond futures contract ended four basis points up at 118.50 having moved in a narrow 118.55/118.37 range.
Three-month Treasury certificates were yielding 3.04/06 percent against 3.03/06 on Wednesday.
The Belgian franc/mark rate was 20.5850/70 from Wednesday's 20.5835/45.
